articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually dropped AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like it's a recipe for banana bread. The irony of America's cybersecurity agency leaking its own crown jewels is so thick you could cut it with a rusty SSH key.

articles.title: 23andMe inherits lawsuit over 'disturbing' DNA data breach
articles.summary: Critical RCE in Gogs has been sitting unfixed since March while maintainers ghost the researcher who found it. Nothing says 'responsible disclosure' like radio silence and a public exploit module.

articles.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface
articles.summary: Palo Alto's GlobalProtect authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0257) is being actively exploited in the wild. Because nothing protects like bypassing the protection entirely.

articles.title: Dutch cops wrest 17M devices from mystery botnet's clutches
articles.summary: 23andMe facing lawsuit over their 2023 mega-breach where they allegedly downplayed the leak while secretly paying ransom. Your DNA data: priceless to science, cheap to hackers.

articles.title: 6 million Carnival Cruise customers’ data impacted amid hacker group’s slew of breaches
articles.summary: Disgruntled bug hunter 'humiliated' by Microsoft promises a 'bone shattering drop' of zero-days. Hell hath no fury like a vulnerability researcher scorned by Redmond's bureaucracy.

articles.title: Lawmakers Demand Answers as CISA Tries to Contain Data Leak
articles.summary: Netherlands seizes 800 servers and arrests two hosting company owners for enabling Russian cyberattacks. Sometimes the best defense is a good old-fashioned server raid.

articles.title: More License Plate Reader Mission Creep: School Residency Verification, Background Checks, and Noise Complaints
articles.summary: Age verification systems are creating a privacy nightmare for everyone in the name of protecting children. Because nothing says 'safety' like requiring a drivers license to read Twitter.

articles.title: 🔒 A Win for Encrypted Messaging | EFFector 38.10
articles.summary: Police are using license plate readers for everything from school residency checks to noise complaints. Mission creep meets surveillance state in a beautiful dystopian waltz.

articles.title: CISA Admin Leaked AWS GovCloud Keys on Github
articles.summary: 23-year-old Ottawa man arrested for building Kimwolf botnet that enslaved millions of IoT devices. Your smart toaster was probably part of his DDoS army and you never even knew.

articles.title: Ask Paul: May 29 ⭐
articles.summary: Canada's Bill C-22 lawful access legislation is being rushed through despite being 'badly designed, badly explained, badly consulted.' Government surveillance with the quality control of a gas station sushi bar.
